Hi! I’m interested in working on #696, but I’d like to clarify its intended scope.

Should I only restate the two nearby inclusion lemmas,

mRed_of_parallelReduction
parallelReduction_of_red

using relation inequalities, for example

ParallelReduction ≤ ReflTransGen Red
Red ≤ ParallelReduction

and then update reflTransGen_parallelReduction_mRed accordingly?

Or does “and others” mean that I should also search for similar inclusion lemmas elsewhere in cslib and restate those? Should the existing theorem names be preserved?

Hi! I meant the latter, I was thinking of lamba calculus also. In Mathlib it seems that there are now pairs of theorems like docs#Relation.reflGen_le_reflTransGen and docs#Relation.ReflGen.to_reflTransGen, where the latter is an intentional pointwise version for convenience. So I guess at minimum we could just add all the ≤ versions of these theorems and then decide if the originals are worth keeping? We also typically use the notations for reductions, so maybe writing mRed_of_parallelReduction as (· ⭢ₚ ·) ≤ (· ↠ ·) like in the docstring is more legible?

Regarding naming, we don't (yet) follow a strict policy of deprecation like Mathlib, so fixing names is welcome. (mRed as an example refers to an API that no longer exists!) In general we try to follow the more obvious naming Mathlib conventions, but especially some of the older lamba calculus modules I wrote very early on aren't great about this. (I'd love for someone to systematically do renaming of these modules, I just haven't found the time)

Thanks, that clears it up. I guess I’ll add ≤ versions for the two SKI lemmas and for step_to_para/para_to_redex, keep the pointwise versions for now, and leave broader renaming to a separate PR. Are these four the intended scope for #696?

Chris Henson said:

In Mathlib it seems that there are now pairs of theorems like docs#Relation.reflGen_le_reflTransGen and docs#Relation.ReflGen.to_reflTransGen, where the latter is an intentional pointwise version for convenience.

FWIW you don't have to have two versions, if you namespace the ≤ version then dot-notation works fine:

import Mathlib
namespace Relation
variable {α : Type*} {r : α → α → Prop}

theorem ReflGen.le_reflTransGen : ReflGen r ≤ ReflTransGen r :=
  reflGen_le_reflTransGen

variable {a b : α} (h : ReflGen r a b)

-- dot-notation works
#check h.le_reflTransGen
Yeah that makes sense to me. But I'm not sure if this will lose some compatibility?
I see, then I suppose we should follow this pattern and not have these "duplicate" theorems. @Snir Broshi are you planning to eventually make such a change in Mathlib?

No, since this was rejected during the review of #30526, though I'd guess opinions differ between reviewers.
But since this isn't mathlib I wanted to point out that the duplication is superfluous. I think the duplication is strange, but idk.

Mildly off-topic for here, but I think in the Mathlib context it would be worth opening a PR that removes just this duplication. When I saw that discussion in the review of #30526, I did not feel it was a hard rejection of the idea of removing this duplication, but an artifact of there being a few moving parts to that PR.

The duplication wasn't removed, it was added because a reviewer asked for it to be duplicated.
Removing it in a separate PR might work, but it feels sneaky.
I'm not asking to be "sneaky" in any way: in such a PR I would clearly link to the previous discussion and tag the reviewer.
